population.note: City-proper and metro figures are approximate estimates pending Census reconciliation. Clark County unincorporated areas (much of the actual built-up Las Vegas Valley, including the Strip itself) fall outside city-proper limits, which understates the city's functional footprint relative to its metro population.

visitWindow.note: Trip 1 stop between Salt Lake City and Phoenix; guide built retroactively as control-group data against Trip 2's sourced-curation cities. Punk Rock Bowling festival (late May) falls well outside this window and is included only as scene-context citation.

framing: Las Vegas is a company town that happens to be the most surveilled, most photographed tourist product in America -- but underneath the Strip is a genuine desert city: a downtown arts district built out of a converted 1998 warehouse, the strongest union local in the country (Culinary Workers Union Local 226), a volunteer-run hackerspace, and a museum that NOFX's Fat Mike built out of Kurt Cobain's couch. This guide deliberately routes around the casino floor, prioritizing Fremont East, the 18b Arts District, Chinatown/Filipinotown, and the city's own DIY-punk and labor-organizing histories over Strip-branded attractions.

analyticalThread.summary: Founded 1935, now Nevada's largest union at 60,000 members -- called 'America's greatest modern labor success story' by The New Republic. In a right-to-work state, roughly 97% of bargaining units voluntarily join and pay dues; the union has driven Democratic turnout in every Nevada election since 2016 and won a 32% wage increase in its 2023 casino contract plus a 69-day strike victory at Virgin Hotels (Nov 2024-Jan 2025). This is a NEW candidate thread proposed by this run, distinct from the existing 'radical-political-geography' Western-leg thread (Boise's Frank Church/Anne Frank Memorial, Salt Lake City's Bill Haywood/IWW) in that it documents contemporary, ongoing labor power rather than historical civil-liberties memory. Flagging for the coordinator to decide whether this merges into radical-political-geography or stands alone -- do not write to the Trip Route and Threads doc directly per this run's instructions.

locations.name: The Bellagio
locations.address: 3600 S Las Vegas Blvd, Las Vegas, NV
locations.note: Primary filming location — casino floor, botanical gardens, art gallery, Dale Chihuly glass lobby ceiling, and the fountain finale.

locations.name: Palms Casino Resort
locations.note: Palme d'Or and Best Picture winner (5 Oscars total). Filmed here and on Fremont Street; plot centers on an impulsive Vegas elopement.

locations.name: Caesars Palace
locations.note: Filming location, also used for Rain Man (1988) and Hangover Part III (2013).

notablePeople.name: Jenna Jameson
notablePeople.note: Daughter of a Folies Bergère showgirl and a Las Vegas Sheriff's Dept officer; began dancing in Vegas strip clubs as a teenager in 1991.

notablePeople.name: Brandon Flowers
notablePeople.note: Frontman of The Killers. Sam's Town (2006) and Battle Born (2012, named for the Nevada flag) are explicit odes to Nevada; called Vegas 'the lion's den.'

notablePeople.name: Brendon Urie
notablePeople.note: Panic! at the Disco formed among Summerlin high schoolers in 2004.

notablePeople.name: Dan Reynolds
notablePeople.note: Frontman of Imagine Dragons; the band relocated to and was based in his hometown to record its first three EPs.

recommendations.name: The Writer's Block
recommendations.address: 519 S 6th St, Las Vegas, NV
recommendations.note: Downtown's flagship indie bookstore, Las Vegas Weekly's 2025 Readers' Choice Best Bookstore — literary fiction, poetry, deep Nevada-authors section, Onyx Coffee Lab built in, 2-4 events weekly.

source.detail: Las Vegas Weekly, Smart Vegas Deals

recommendations.name: Amber Unicorn Books
recommendations.address: 2202 W Charleston Blvd #5, Las Vegas, NV
recommendations.note: Warehouse-style used bookstore, 60,000+ books at $1–5, sourced via estate sales and a walk-in buying program — genuine treasure-hunt browsing.

recommendations.name: Dead Poet Books
recommendations.address: 937 S Rainbow Blvd #107, Las Vegas, NV
recommendations.note: Small, tightly curated used shop — literary fiction, poetry, rare and signed first editions.

recommendations.name: Get Booked
recommendations.address: 4640 Paradise Rd, Las Vegas, NV
recommendations.note: Vegas's only gay-owned LGBTQ+ retail bookstore since 1993 — part bookshop, part community fixture, queer fiction alongside its adult-shop inventory.

recommendations.name: The Book Cellar
recommendations.note: Academic used-book shop near UNLV — textbooks, scholarly presses, discount research texts. Modest fifth pick, included for completeness.

recommendations.name: Vinyl Threat @ The Punk Rock Museum
recommendations.address: 1422 Western Ave, Las Vegas, NV
recommendations.note: The museum's in-house record shop, punk vinyl tied to the archive, plus rare demos pressed exclusively on the shop's own TPRM ODs label.

source.detail: The Punk Rock Museum, Rebel Atlas

recommendations.name: 11th Street Records
recommendations.address: 1023 E Fremont St, Las Vegas, NV
recommendations.note: A working part of the local music ecosystem downtown, with an in-store studio hosting live sessions, tied into East Fremont's smaller venues.

recommendations.name: Cash 4 Chaos
recommendations.address: 4110 S Maryland Pkwy, Suites 27 & 28, Las Vegas, NV
recommendations.note: Punk/metal specialist since 1998, blending records with band shirts, patches, and scene ephemera — built by lifers, not trend forecasters.

recommendations.name: Primitive Recordings
recommendations.address: 3441 W Sahara Ave, Suite B-7, Las Vegas, NV
recommendations.note: Metal/horror/sci-fi specialist carrying extreme metal, underground shirts, and tapes not always available online.

recommendations.name: Wax Trax Records
recommendations.address: 2909 S Decatur Blvd, Las Vegas, NV
recommendations.note: A three-floor operation for serious crate-diggers — the broad, well-known pick alongside the punk/metal specialists above.

recommendations.name: PublicUs
recommendations.address: 1126 Fremont St, Las Vegas, NV
recommendations.note: Downtown's hybrid café-marketplace — pour-over and Japanese iced coffee, plus an honey toast and elevated brunch program.

recommendations.name: Vesta Coffee Roasters
recommendations.note: A no-pretense specialty roaster — smooth espresso, strong cold brew and cortado program.

recommendations.name: Gäbi Coffee & Bakery
recommendations.address: 5808 Spring Mountain Rd #104, Las Vegas, NV
recommendations.note: A discreet, minimally signed Korean-inspired café with vintage décor, lavender latte and matcha affogato, real pastry program.

recommendations.name: Sunrise Coffee
recommendations.address: 3130 E Sunset Rd, Las Vegas, NV
recommendations.note: Dog-friendly, mismatched-furniture neighborhood shop in East Vegas — house chai, vegan pastry case.

recommendations.name: Bad Owl Coffee
recommendations.address: 8035 S Rainbow Blvd #100, Las Vegas, NV
recommendations.note: A themed South Vegas café (butterbeer latte, lavender latte) that leans into novelty without sacrificing the coffee.

recommendations.name: Freed's Bakery
recommendations.note: Operating since 1959 — cannoli filled to order, sfogliatelle, Italian cookies, the city's default custom-cake maker. Not casino-owned.

recommendations.name: Chloé Patisserie
recommendations.note: Paris-trained pastry chef, kouign-amann/canelé/opera cake — reportedly where hotel pastry chefs go on their own days off.

recommendations.name: Bread & Butter Bakery Cafe
recommendations.note: Naturally leavened 24-hour sourdough with no commercial yeast, plus weekend sourdough cinnamon rolls — sells out by 1pm.

recommendations.name: Great Buns Bakery
recommendations.note: Hong Kong-style BBQ pork buns, egg tarts, pineapple buns — time it around the fresh-batch window.

recommendations.name: Kona Bakery
recommendations.note: Japanese shokupan milk bread, curry buns, melon pan, matcha croissants. Closed Wednesdays.

recommendations.name: Shrimp Cocktail — originally Golden Gate Hotel, now Circa Resort
recommendations.note: Invented by Golden Gate owner Italo Ghelfi in 1959 as a 50¢ loss-leader inspired by San Francisco's Fisherman's Wharf. Discontinued 2017, briefly revived 2019, now lives at owner Derek Stevens' Circa Resort.

source.detail: TasteAtlas — Best Dishes in Las Vegas

recommendations.name: Filet Mignon — The Golden Steer
recommendations.note: Open since 1958, the Rat Pack's steakhouse of choice — aged prime filet in a mid-century dining room.

recommendations.name: French Toast Ambrosia — The Peppermill Fireside Lounge
recommendations.note: A since-1972 retro Vegas diner landmark — vanilla-cinnamon French toast, fresh fruit, whipped cream, blueberry syrup, sunken fire-pit lounge.

recommendations.name: Adobada Tacos — Tacos El Gordo
recommendations.note: Tijuana-style al pastor tacos, hand-pressed tortillas, house salsas — the late-night Vegas standard.

recommendations.name: Filipino Food — Filipinotown
recommendations.note: Clark County's officially designated Filipinotown, reflecting roughly 250,000 Filipino residents in the valley — one of the densest, least-touristed food scenes in the city.

recommendations.name: Ethel M Chocolates
recommendations.note: Handmade chocolates from a Henderson factory with an attached cactus garden — genuinely locally made, not a Strip gift-shop label.

recommendations.name: JoJo's Jerky
recommendations.note: Nevada jerky maker since 2004, no preservatives — an easy, genuinely shelf-stable mailable gift.

recommendations.name: Al Bees Nevada Honey
recommendations.note: Raw honey from Sierra Nevada apiaries — the direct bees-interest pick.

recommendations.name: Savor Spice Co.
recommendations.note: Black woman-owned artisanal spice-blend maker — a distinctive mailable gift beyond the generic Vegas hot sauce.

recommendations.name: The Mob Museum's House Moonshine
recommendations.note: 100-proof corn moonshine distilled in-house at The Underground, the museum's working speakeasy/distillery exhibit, sold retail through local liquor stores since 2019.

recommendations.name: The Neon Museum
recommendations.address: 770 N Las Vegas Blvd, Las Vegas, NV
recommendations.filmConnection: Casino (1995), Mars Attacks! (1996), Last Vegas (2013) — La Concha Motel lobby / boneyard
recommendations.note: A boneyard of ~250 vintage casino signs dating to the 1930s; the salvaged La Concha Motel lobby is now the visitor center. 'Brilliant!' relights unlit signs after dark.

recommendations.name: Atomic Liquors
recommendations.filmConnection: Casino (1995) production base; also appears in The Hangover (2009) and a Twilight Zone episode
recommendations.note: Opened 1954, popularly claimed as the oldest freestanding bar in Vegas. Scorsese's Casino crew used the garage next door as a production studio.

recommendations.name: Pinball Hall of Fame
recommendations.note: Nonprofit, volunteer-run hands-on museum with 700+ playable machines at 25¢ a pop; excess revenue goes to the Salvation Army. Founder Tim Arnold has collected since 1972.

recommendations.name: Seven Magic Mountains
recommendations.district: Ivanpah Valley, S. Las Vegas Blvd
recommendations.note: Ugo Rondinone's Day-Glo stacked-boulder land art installation — $3.5M, one of the largest US land-art works completed in the last 40 years, extended through May 2027.

recommendations.name: Red Rock Canyon National Conservation Area
recommendations.note: Sandstone walls up to 3,000 ft, a 13-mile scenic loop, hiking and rock climbing. The Killers publicly opposed development here in 2017.

recommendations.name: Springs Preserve
recommendations.note: 180 acres on Las Vegas's original water source — desert-sustainability demonstration site, botanical gardens, wetland trails, opened 2007.

recommendations.name: Culinary Workers Union Local 226 (Headquarters)
recommendations.note: Founded 1935, now Nevada's largest union at 60,000 members — 'America's greatest modern labor success story' per The New Republic, and the single most concrete leftist political anchor in the city.

recommendations.name: The Mob Museum
recommendations.note: Housed in the city's actual 1933 federal courthouse, with the restored Kefauver hearing courtroom and a working in-house speakeasy/distillery.

recommendations.name: Double Down Saloon
recommendations.address: 4640 Paradise Rd, Las Vegas, NV
recommendations.note: Founded 1992 by P Moss in the old Fruit Loop district; no-cover punk, garage, ska, surf, and psychobilly every night, a Bourdain favorite.

recommendations.name: The Punk Rock Museum / Triple Down
recommendations.address: 1422 Western Ave, Las Vegas, NV
recommendations.note: Founded 2023 by NOFX's Fat Mike and Lisa Brownlee, governed by a 10-person collective incl. Pat Smear and Tony Hawk; playable-instrument Jam Room, chapel, Triple Down dive bar built in.

recommendations.name: Backstage Bar & Billiards
recommendations.note: Books electronic/glitch/experimental lineups alongside standard rock bills; one of Punk Rock Bowling's official venue stages.

recommendations.name: Fremont Country Club
recommendations.note: A mid-size downtown room, one of Punk Rock Bowling's core venues — verify current booking calendar before visiting.

recommendations.name: Punk Rock Bowling & Music Festival
recommendations.note: Founded 1999 by Youth Brigade's Stern brothers (BYO Records); Memorial Day weekend, 8,000-10,000/day across downtown venues. Falls outside this trip's Oct window — scene-context citation, not a bookable activity.

recommendations.name: The Neon Museum Gift Shop
recommendations.note: Postcards and magnets designed from the museum's own vintage sign collection — genuinely tied to Vegas's specific visual heritage.

recommendations.name: The Arts Factory (18b Arts District)
recommendations.address: 107 E Charleston Blvd, Las Vegas, NV
recommendations.note: Wes Myles's 1998 warehouse conversion that founded the Arts District; galleries inside sell local-artist prints and small-run goods, especially on First Friday.

recommendations.name: The Punk Rock Museum Gift Shop
recommendations.address: 1422 Western Ave, Las Vegas, NV
recommendations.note: Patches, pins, and postcards designed in-house, tied to the museum's flyer-art aesthetic.

recommendations.name: The Writer's Block
recommendations.address: 519 S 6th St, Las Vegas, NV
recommendations.note: Nevada-author titles and small literary prints — a better souvenir than a shot glass.

recommendations.name: Springs Preserve Gift Shop
recommendations.note: Desert-themed, native-seed-packet, education-nonprofit-adjacent gifts tied to the preserve's sustainability mission.

recommendations.name: SYN Shop
recommendations.address: 5967 Harrison Dr, Suite 1, Las Vegas, NV 89120
recommendations.note: Las Vegas's community hackerspace/makerspace — member-run space for hackers, makers, and inventors with an explicit mentorship culture; check their Discord for current open hours.

recommendations.name: Cowtown Guitars (historical, closed 2019)
recommendations.note: Not a current pick — flagged for context only. A nationally known vintage guitar shop (an authenticated 1963 Hendrix Strat passed through here) that relocated to the Arts District in 2011 and closed in 2019.

statusNotes.text: The original 50¢ Golden Gate Hotel shrimp cocktail was discontinued in 2017 when Du-par's closed; owner Derek Stevens briefly revived it in 2019 and it now lives on at his Circa Resort instead of the Golden Gate.
Cowtown Guitars, once a nationally known vintage-guitar landmark in the downtown Arts District, closed in 2019. Listed for historical context only, not as a visitable pick.
Punk Rock Bowling & Music Festival runs Memorial Day weekend (late May), well outside this trip's Oct 9–13, 2025 window. Included as a scene-context citation, not a bookable October activity.
Fremont Country Club's current booking calendar could not be directly verified this run (site fetch blocked) — confirm lineup before visiting.

honestGaps.text: The mandatory anarchist/radical/infoshop bookstore search turned up no Las Vegas storefront — no equivalent of Salt Lake City's Boing! Anarchist Collective or Oklahoma City's Literati Press co-op. The city's leftist political infrastructure runs through the Culinary Workers Union Local 226 (see sights) rather than a bookstore-anchored infoshop scene.

Category 10 carries 2 picks, not 5. Unlike Salt Lake City (Squarewave Sound) or Oklahoma City (Keeley Electronics), Las Vegas does not appear to have a currently operating dedicated synth/pedal boutique or electronics-surplus storefront — repeated searches surfaced only national chains (Guitar Center). SYN Shop is the one genuine, verifiable DIY-electronics anchor; Cowtown Guitars, the closest historical analogue, closed in 2019. Padding to five would misrepresent the city.

scopeDecision: Las Vegas-proper and unincorporated Clark County Valley (Henderson, Summerlin, Paradise) treated as one functional city, since the Strip itself and much of the built-up valley sit outside Las Vegas city-proper limits — flagged in population.note rather than silently conflated.
